question: Which of the following compounds of carbon does NOT exist?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CH6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CH6** does not exist because it is not possible to have six hydrogen atoms bonded to a single carbon atom under normal conditions.
 
• The carbon atom can form a maximum of four covalent bonds due to its tetravalency, adhering to the octet rule.
 
• Common carbon compounds include **CH4 (methane)**, **C2H6 (ethane)**, and **C6H6 (benzene)**, all of which follow the valency rules of carbon.
 
• In the case of **CH4**, carbon forms four single bonds with hydrogen atoms, while in **C2H6**, each carbon atom forms three single bonds with hydrogen and one single bond with another carbon atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Octet Rule**

 
 
• A chemical rule of thumb that reflects the observation that atoms of main-group elements tend to combine in such a way that each atom has eight electrons in its valence shell.
 
• This rule is a guiding principle for understanding the bonding behavior of atoms.
 
 
 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon**
 
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons and thus can form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This property allows carbon to form a wide variety of complex organic molecules.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Structures**
 
 
• The structure of a molecule is determined by the arrangement of its atoms and the bonds between them.
 
• Methane (CH4) has a tetrahedral structure, while benzene (C6H6) has a planar hexagonal structure with alternating double bonds.
 
 
 
• **Hybridization**
 
 
• The concept of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds.
 
• For example, in methane (CH4), carbon undergoes sp3 hybridization to form four equivalent bonds with hydrogen atoms.
